gallery.source: Aerial view of the Union Iron Works, San Francisco, California (USA), circa in 1918 (NH 42535)
gallery.description:
Aerial view of the Union Iron Works, San Francisco, California (USA), photographed during World War I, with four-piper destroyers under construction at the Risdon Iron Works in the lower right. Four submarines and one destroyer hull in dry-dock are at the piers in the center, along with some large merchant ships. Risdon, part of Union, is to the lower right of the ink line.

gallery.artist: Image is from 1918 booklet published by Bethlehem Shipbuilding Corporation LTD, Charles M. Schwab director. pages 97 - 98. Published on the completion of the 1917 Frederick Meyer Renaissance Revival Bethlehem office building on the corner of Illinois and 20th Streets. Published by Bethlehem Shipbuilding and Steel Corporation LTD. General Offices Bethlehem, PA. Branch offices 111 Broadway, New York, N.Y. 260 California Street San Francisco, Cal. Prints were widely distributed, you can see one framed at the RAMP, a bar across the water from Pier 70. 855 Terry A Francois Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94158. 99.101.143.78 hank chapot 99.101.143.78

gallery.filename: USS Kidder (DD-319), USS Selfridge (DD-320), USS Chase (DD-323), USS Mervine (DD-322), USS Marcus (DD-321), USS La Vallette (DD-315) and USS Yarborough (DD-314) fitting out at Union Iron Works, San Francisco (USA) on 1 April 1920 (19-LC-38-L-3).jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Kidder (DD-319), USS Selfridge (DD-320), USS Chase (DD-323), USS Mervine (DD-322), USS Marcus (DD-321), USS La Vallette (DD-315) and USS Yarborough (DD-314) fitting out at Union Iron Works, San Francisco (USA) on 1 April 1920 (19-LC-38-L-3).jpg
gallery.description:
U.S. Navy destroyers fitting out, at the Bethlehem Shipbuilding Corporation's Union Iron Works, San Francisco, California (USA), on 1 April 1920. Ships present are (from left to right):
USS Kidder (DD-319),
USS Selfridge (DD-320),
USS Chase (DD-323),
USS Mervine (DD-322),
USS Marcus (DD-321),
USS La Vallette (DD-315) and
USS Yarborough (DD-314).
